_how_to_add: To add a project card, append one object to "projects" below and rebuild (python -B build.py). Fields: id (kebab-case), name, status (live | building | idea), kicker (3 to 6 words), summary (1 to 3 sentences), skills (list), proof (list of {label, href}; href is a page of this site or omitted), links (list of {label, href}; only https links you are happy to publish). Everything here is published, so keep private names and people out. The site tests check this file for private wording; run scan/privacy-scan.ps1 on dist before any publish.
intro: One place to see what I build, how I decide, and what I can prove. Each project below states what is real, what is synthetic and what is still unproven.

skills.detail: Permissions on the tool, not the model. Dry-run, approval, undo and a tamper-evident audit log. Prompt-injection tripwire with a separate hard control.
Python orchestration with PowerShell actions through a fail-closed bridge, schema checked on both sides.
Baseline checks over Graph-shaped data, joiner and leaver plans, requester verification, rollback from recorded before-state.
Every claim points at a test. Every unknown is labelled. Demo commands are run by a test.
A static, accessible site with no third-party requests, light and dark themes, built from real runs of the code.
Specs before code, change notes per item, decisions written down, independent review before merge.

projects.name: Redline
projects.summary: An AI and automation program for a managed service provider, built as runnable, tested software. Small tested scripts do the work. A model only suggests which one to press, and every action is dry-run first, approved by a lead and written to a hash-chained log.
